sources.title: Elicitation
sources.document_status: Official historical dated specification. URL mode marked new and subject to change.

evidence.fact: Form accept submits data; decline explicitly refuses; cancel dismisses without a decision.
Only declared modes apply. Clients identify the requester, offer decline/cancel, permit form review, and obtain navigation consent.

evidence.section: URL Mode Elicitation Requests; Safe URL Handling
evidence.fact: Sensitive input uses external URL mode. Show full URL and host; keep user inputs outside client/model access.

evidence.section: Completion Notifications for URL Mode Elicitation
evidence.fact: URL acceptance is consent, not completion. Completion IDs match the originating elicitation; unknown or completed IDs are ignored.

evidence.section: URL Elicitation Required Error; Security Considerations
evidence.fact: An error may list several required URL elicitations. Requests bind to client/user identity. Third-party authorization differs from MCP access authorization.

sources.boundary: The protocol chooses no specific UI. It supplies no general action-permission or proposal-revision approval contract.

sources.title: Cancellation

evidence.fact: Ordinary cancellation identifies an outstanding request issued in the same direction. A receiver may ignore unknown, completed, or uncancellable requests.
Task-augmented work uses tasks/cancel instead. Application UI should indicate cancellation was requested.

sources.boundary: A fire-and-forget cancellation notification proves neither remote acceptance nor stopped side effects.

sources.title: Tasks
sources.document_status: Official experimental feature in a historical dated revision.

evidence.fact: Task support and task cancellation are capabilities; individual tools may require, allow, or forbid tasks.

evidence.section: Task ID Requirements; Associating Task-Related Messages
evidence.fact: Receiver-generated task IDs identify tasks. Related input requests share that task identity; task operations target their explicit taskId.
A valid cancel response follows transition to cancelled; execution stopping remains best-effort. Terminal tasks reject cancellation. Cancelled state stays terminal even if execution continues.
Where authorization context exists, tasks and operations bind to that context.

sources.boundary: A cancelled task state does not certify physical interruption, reversal, or absence of side effects. The protocol defines no universal steering acknowledgment.

atlas_proposals.title: Preserve decision intent
atlas_proposals.proposed_contract: Mark each pending item as an information request, an authority grant, or an external handoff. Use distinct submitted, declined, and dismissed outcomes. State the action, requester, and scope. A response to one item must not silently resolve another.
atlas_proposals.additive_to_existing_P0: Decision meaning and scope, rather than another generic uncertain-outcome rule.

atlas_proposals.title: Keep outstanding decisions independently addressable
atlas_proposals.proposed_contract: Retain a visible pending count and a stable item per unresolved decision. Bind response controls to the originating work, requester/account, and decision identity. Resolve only the matching item; preserve the others.
atlas_proposals.illustrative_acceptance_case: Two pending decisions from different work items remain independently actionable after the first is answered.
atlas_proposals.additive_to_existing_P0: Multiple outstanding decisions and response targeting.

atlas_proposals.title: Distinguish an external handoff from completion
atlas_proposals.proposed_contract: Before opening an external flow, show its destination and purpose. After consent, show awaiting external completion. Keep retry, dismiss, or resume controls available when the application supports them.
atlas_proposals.additive_to_existing_P0: The specific consent-to-navigate boundary, not generic lost-reply recovery.

atlas_proposals.title: Acknowledge steering without overstating its effect
atlas_proposals.classification: Atlas application-contract proposal; not prescribed by MCP
atlas_proposals.proposed_contract: Attach steering to the intended active work. Distinguish sent, received, and applied/rejected acknowledgment only where the runtime supplies evidence. If interruption is unsupported, explain the effective boundary. Confirming protocol cancellation must not imply rollback.
atlas_proposals.additive_to_existing_P0: Steering applicability and acknowledgment vocabulary. General cancellation races remain in existing P0.

atlas_proposals.title: Bind approval to the proposal the user reviewed
atlas_proposals.classification: Atlas application-contract proposal; evidence gap in these sources
atlas_proposals.proposed_contract: Show which proposal and revision a decision authorizes. On material scope changes, invalidate the old decision and surface the changed proposal for review. Record authority scope separately from ordinary submitted information.
atlas_proposals.boundary: MCP establishes request/task identity and contextual authorization, not proposal hashes, revision binding, universal approval policy, or steering semantics.
atlas_proposals.additive_to_existing_P0: Inherited/reused proposal-revision consent from existing P0 and the original Agent Experience chapter; not a new contribution.

non_goals: No instruction to install MCP, adopt its transport, write a backend, or implement its wire vocabulary.
No claim that all agents support MCP, elicitation, tasks, cancel, concurrent decisions, or steering.
No duplication of Atlas P0 general lost replies, cancellation races, stale status, or uncertain outcomes.
No repository or global policy mutation.
